>I think this makes sense as we don't do much physics processing in the Editor for this to be enabled, but I'd love some opinion

Depends on what you're doing. I'm working on a project that exclusively runs physics-based simulations in the editor. 

I think it would make more sense to implement this comment in the issue you linked: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/94106#issuecomment-2215508064

Which is to use the regular process by default, but fallback to using the physics process when using multithreading (at the sacrifice of smoothness when using high refresh rate monitors). 

Edit: You could probably combine the two and have the editor hint be optional, so you still have multi-threading in the runtime, and smoothness in the editor, but also multithreading in the editor if desired with the fallback.
